messages:
sara (runtime): Quick heads-up — noticed a ~12% p95 regression on smoke workload after yesterday's scheduler heuristics change. baseline vs head on small-batch (B=1..4) only. :eyes:

javier (infra): ugh, saw alerts too. any obvious traces?

elaine (bench): I ran a couple of perfetto + nsys captures on a repro run (same model, seq=128). attaching links: https://perf.ci/trace/2524201999-before.html and https://perf.ci/trace/2524201999-after.html

perf-ci-bot: nsys profile completed: https://perf.ci/nsys/2524201999-after.qdrep (size=120MB)

mike (ml): can you paste the hot timeline snippet? curious if kernel choice flipped.

elaine (bench): pasted small excerpt below (from perfetto flame):
```
[before] timeline: matmul_fast_kernel 8.2ms -> kv_read 0.6ms -> softmax 1.1ms
[after ] timeline: matmul_generic_kernel 31.4ms -> kv_read 0.6ms -> softmax 1.1ms
```
Looks like matmul kernel selector picked generic path after heuristic tweak.

javier (infra): That aligns with what I saw in the nsys call stacks — kernel selector returned fallback variant for certain sequence-length/batch combos. nvtx markers show selector decision at runtime.

sara (runtime): Which commit changed the heuristic? I remember a tweak landed yesterday that increases batching window to try to coalesce more requests. Commit hash maybe f3a2b9c?

javier (infra): Ran git bisect locally, narrowed to range: f3000..f3a2b9c. The actual culprit is f3a2b9c39: "increase coalescing_window to 6ms, prefer latency-stable kernels".

elaine (bench): Bisect trace comparison (before vs after) attached. Key diff: kernel_selector::score() now biases away from specialized small-batch kernel when coalescing_window > 4ms. For our microbench small-batch path that penalizes the specialized matmul.

mike (ml): Why would increasing coalescing window cause the selector to prefer generic kernel? I'd expect more batching to favor fast matmul.

javier (infra): Because selector uses estimated steady-state batch distribution — when coalescing_window is larger, the estimator predicts occasional B=8 spikes, and generic_kernel has more stable throughput at that simulated distribution. The estimator math had an off-by-factor that overweighted latency variance.

sara (runtime): Repro steps I ran:
```
# before (good)
./tools/run_inference --model llama-13b --batch=1 --seq_len=128 --profile perfetto_before.html
nsys profile --output nsys_before --trace=nvtx ./bin/serve --workload small_batch

# after (bad)
./tools/run_inference --model llama-13b --batch=1 --seq_len=128 --profile perfetto_after.html
nsys profile --output nsys_after --trace=nvtx ./bin/serve --workload small_batch
```
The flame diffs show kernel switch at iteration ~120.

elaine (bench): I also captured KV cache stats. Before: cache hit ratio 98.6%, after: 94.2% — there's a tiny eviction spike around same time as kernel change. That worsens performance because generic kernel does more memory work.

mike (ml): So two interacting effects: selector bias and a KV cache thrash happening at the same time. Could the heuristic change have shifted scheduling such that KV prefetch windows misalign?

javier (infra): Exactly. The coalescing_window change altered micro-batching timing which increased contention on the KV cache warmup window. We see evictions at the boundary when batch size flips.

sara (runtime): Proposed fixes:
- revert f3a2b9c (fast) OR
- fix selector scoring: reduce variance weight and add explicit test for small-batch specialized kernel (recommended) OR
- tighten KV prefetch alignment so coalescing doesn't push warmup outside the cache window
Which should we do as hotfix?

elaine (bench): Reverting gives fastest rollback. But longer term, adding unit tests that assert kernel selection for small-batch reproductions is good. I can add a perf regression test that runs the small-batch scenario and checks nvtx-selected kernel name.

mike (ml): +1 for selector fix. The scoring change seems wrong. Happy to help with test vectors to ensure we don't flip back.

javier (infra): I'll open a PR with two commits: 1) small revert patch to restore previous behavior for coalescing_window default, 2) follow-up selector scoring patch with test. Marking rollback as safe.

sara (runtime): Sounds good. Also add CI job using nsys sampling to capture the kernel name in the pipeline (cheap 3-second run). Elaine, can you add perfetto diff link to the PR?

elaine (bench): Yep. I'll include perfetto snapshots + nsys artifacts. Also adding a small script to diff NVTX marker sequences: tools/trace_diff/marker_diff.py (simple grep + compare).

perf-ci-bot: Created issue #1847: "Small-batch regression after coalescing_window change" — https://perf.ci/issues/1847 :fire:

sara (runtime): Great. Thanks team. After PR lands let's run a full A/B: 50k requests production-ish simulation and confirm p50/p95 match baseline. If anything funky remains, we'll run a deeper perfetto + nvprof pass.

javier (infra): timeline for PRs: revert out in 30m, selector fix + tests by EOD.

mike (ml): If anyone needs model-specific baseline numbers I have the training-side traces and microbench harness. Ping me.

elaine (bench): I'll attach the nsys callstack snapshot to the revert PR so reviewers can eyeball kernel names quickly.

sara (runtime): Excellent. Filing retro note for rollout checklist: when tuning coalescing/window heuristics also run small-batch kernel-selection job to catch this interaction. Closing here for now. :white_check_mark:
